title: Object-oriented programming
examples: How is a class different from an object in programming?
Can you give an example of polymorphism in real life?
What is the benefit of using inheritance in large programs?

explain.say: Today we explore object-oriented programming concepts. First we will look at classes and objects.
A class is like a blueprint for creating things. An object is a specific thing built from that blueprint.
Encapsulation means bundling data and methods together. It keeps the internal workings safe from outside changes.
Inheritance allows new classes to take features from existing ones. This promotes code reuse significantly.
Polymorphism means one interface can take many forms. It lets one action work differently for different objects.
In the real world, think about different types of vehicles. They all move, but they move differently.

faq.q: What is the main difference between a class and an object?
faq.a: A class is just the design or template, like a cookie cutter. An object is the actual item created using that template, like the cookie itself.
asks: Are classes and objects the same thing?
What is the difference between definition and instance?

faq.q: How does encapsulation help write better code?
faq.a: It protects the data inside an object from being changed accidentally by other parts of the program. You must use controlled methods to change it.
asks: Why should I hide my variables?
What is data hiding in OOP?

faq.q: Can I inherit from multiple classes?
faq.a: Some languages allow multiple inheritance, but many modern languages prefer composition to avoid complex issues. It is best to stick to single inheritance.
asks: Is it okay to inherit from two parents?
What is the problem with multiple inheritance?

faq.q: What does polymorphism mean in practice?
faq.a: It means you can write one general command, like 'draw', and different objects will know how to draw themselves correctly. A circle draws differently than a square.
asks: How does one action have many forms?

faq.q: When should I use inheritance over composition?
faq.a: Use inheritance when the 'is-a' relationship is very strong, like a 'Dog is an Animal'. Use composition when one thing 'has-a' relationship, like a 'Car has an Engine'.
asks: When is composition preferred in OOP design?

faq.q: If I change the blueprint, do all objects change?
faq.a: No, changing the class blueprint only changes future objects. Existing objects keep the state they had when they were created.
asks: Does changing the class affect existing objects?
Is the state of an object fixed?

facts: A class defines the structure and behavior of an object.
Encapsulation restricts direct access to an object's internal state.
Inheritance models an 'is-a' relationship between classes.
Polymorphism allows objects to respond uniquely to the same message.

quiz.say: If you have a blueprint for a car, what is the blueprint itself called?
quiz.why: The class acts as the template or blueprint defining what the object will look like.

wrong.0: Inheritance is the mechanism of passing traits, not the template itself.
wrong.1: Polymorphism describes the ability to take many forms, not the definition.
wrong.3: An object is the actual item built from the blueprint, not the blueprint itself.

quiz.say: A 'SavingsAccount' class that inherits from a 'BankAccount' class demonstrates which concept?
quiz.why: SavingsAccount gains all the properties and methods of the parent BankAccount class.

wrong.1: Encapsulation is about hiding data, not about inheriting structure.
wrong.2: Polymorphism relates to one action having many forms, not the structure itself.
wrong.3: An object is an instance, whereas the relationship described is between classes.

quiz.say: If you tell a 'Dog' object and a 'Cat' object to 'makeSound()', and they bark and meow respectively, what principle is shown?
quiz.why: Polymorphism allows the single command makeSound() to execute different behaviors based on the object type.

wrong.0: Encapsulation would mean the sound method was hidden and inaccessible.
wrong.1: A class is just the definition; this describes the runtime behavior.
wrong.2: Inheritance shows 'is-a', but this scenario shows varied behavior from one action.
